// Generated from function-catalog.yaml — do not edit manually.
// Re-generate with:
//   cargo run -q -p codegen -- function-catalog.yaml

use crate::value::Value;

/// Combined hash of the catalog + codegen that produced this file.
/// Consumers that pattern-match on generated types should assert
/// against this constant to detect silent schema drift.

/// Generated — do not modify. See top of file.
/// Logical expression tree — value-based, fully recursive.
///
/// Used for normalization and rewrite rules where nested
/// pattern matching is the natural style.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum LogExpr {
    Literal(Value),

    LogicalOr { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    LogicalAnd { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    LogicalNot { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// both params must unify. null input → null output. See null_safe_equal for SQL IS NOT DISTINCT FROM.
    Equal { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// both params must unify. null input → null output. See null_safe_not_equal for SQL IS DISTINCT FROM.
    NotEqual { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    LessThan { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    LessOrEqual { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    GreaterThan { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    GreaterOrEqual { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// no CEL equivalent; lower to LogicalAnd(GreaterOrEqual(x, lo), LessOrEqual(x, hi))
    Between { arg0: Box<LogExpr>, arg1: Box<LogExpr>, arg2: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// SQL null-safe equality (null == null → true). Distinct from Equal which propagates null.
    NullSafeEqual { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// SQL null-safe inequality (null != null → false). Distinct from NotEqual which propagates null.
    NullSafeNotEqual { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// CEL uses has() macro for presence; we likely need this for nullable columns
    IsNull { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    IsNotNull { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// useful for float column guards
    IsNan { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    IsFinite { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// NaN is neither finite nor infinite; IsInfinite != LogicalNot(IsFinite)
    IsInfinite { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// returns first non-null argument. Consumes may_null effect from first operand.
    Coalesce { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// evaluates first operand; if it errors, returns second operand. Consumes may_error effect from first operand. Result may still be nullable (from either branch).
    TryOrElse { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// always evaluates to Err. Return type is bottom (unifies with any T from context). The operand is a string message. Effect is always may_error. Used for explicit user-authored error signaling in CEL scripts. Caught by TryOrElse.
    RaiseError { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    Least { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    Greatest { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// also string/bytes/list concat and timestamp+duration in CEL
    Add { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    Subtract { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    Multiply { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    Divide { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    Negate { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    Modulus { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    Abs { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    Power { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    Sqrt { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    Exp { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    Sign { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    Contains { receiver: Box<LogExpr>, arg: Box<LogExpr> },
    StartsWith { receiver: Box<LogExpr>, arg: Box<LogExpr> },
    EndsWith { receiver: Box<LogExpr>, arg: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// CEL returns bool; Substrait returns the matched substring. Pattern is compiled once if the argument is a literal string; non-literal patterns work but recompile on every evaluation.
    RegexMatch { receiver: Box<LogExpr>, arg: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// Returns the first capture group of the pattern, or null if no match. If the pattern has no capture group, returns the entire match. Pattern is compiled once if the argument is a literal string; non-literal patterns work but recompile on every evaluation.
    RegexExtract { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// Replaces all non-overlapping matches of pattern in the input with the replacement string. Capture group back-references ($1, $2, etc.) are supported in the replacement. Pattern is compiled once if the argument is a literal string; non-literal patterns work but recompile on every evaluation.
    RegexReplace { arg0: Box<LogExpr>, arg1: Box<LogExpr>, arg2: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// Zero-based path segment of a URL or URL reference, e.g. url_path_segment("https://h/a/b/c", 1) is "b". The third argument selects a parse mode: "auto" (also the meaning of a null mode) accepts authority-less references such as "/foo/bar.php?baz=quux"; "require_scheme" accepts only absolute URLs; "require_authority" additionally requires a non-empty host. Returns null when the input does not satisfy the mode, the URL cannot carry a path, the index is negative or past the last segment, or the mode string is unrecognized. A literal mode is a candidate for literal-argument specialization.
    UrlPathSegment { arg0: Box<LogExpr>, arg1: Box<LogExpr>, arg2: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// First value of a URL query parameter by name, percent-decoded per the WHATWG form-urlencoded rules, e.g. url_query_param("https://h/p?a=1&b=2", "b") is "2". The third argument is the same parse mode as url_path_segment ("auto" when null). Returns null when the input does not satisfy the mode or the parameter is absent; an explicitly empty value ("?a=") is the empty string, not null.
    UrlQueryParam { arg0: Box<LogExpr>, arg1: Box<LogExpr>, arg2: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// also maps to Substrait octet_length for bytes, and list/map cardinality
    Size { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    Lower { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    Upper { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    Substring { arg0: Box<LogExpr>, arg1: Box<LogExpr>, arg2: Box<LogExpr> },
    Replace { arg0: Box<LogExpr>, arg1: Box<LogExpr>, arg2: Box<LogExpr> },
    Trim { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    StringSplit { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    StringPosition { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// in CEL this is the _+_ operator on strings
    Concat { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// CEL splits into per-component methods; we unify as extract(component, ts)
    TimestampExtract { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// useful for time bucketing in predicates
    RoundTemporal { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    RoundCalendar { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    CurrentTimestamp,
    CastBool { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    CastInt { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    CastUint { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    CastDouble { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    CastString { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    CastBytes { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    CastDuration { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    CastTimestamp { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    TypeOf { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// type-checker hint only; no runtime effect
    Dyn { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    Conditional { condition: Box<LogExpr>, then_expr: Box<LogExpr>, else_expr: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// also works as map(K, V)[K] → V; overloaded
    Index { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    In { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// The list with one element added at the end. A CEL list literal whose items are not all constants lowers to a chain of these starting from the empty list, so `[a, b]` is list_append(list_append([], a), b).
    ListAppend { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// Elements of the first list followed by elements of the second. CEL spells this `_+_` on lists, an overload of the arithmetic operator that is not yet distinguished from it.
    ListConcat { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// Concatenation of the inner lists, in order. One level only. An inner element that is not a list contributes nothing. flat_map is flatten(map(xs, x, f(x))).
    Flatten { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// The elements of a list, in order. Any other value (including null and maps) yields the empty list. Identity on lists; exists so a selection over a value of unknown shape can be written without a type test.
    ListElements { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// The member values of a map, in key order. Any other value (including null and lists) yields the empty list.
    MapValues { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// The value itself followed by every value nested inside it, depth-first in document order (list elements in order, map member values in key order). Always non-empty: a scalar yields a one-element list of itself.
    Descendants { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// Optional list element: a one-element list holding the element at the given index, counting from the end when negative, or the empty list if the index is out of range or the first argument is not a list. The list counterpart of get_child_by_index; maps use get_member_by_key.
    GetElementByIndex { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// Optional map member: a one-element list holding the value of the member whose key equals the second argument, or the empty list if there is no such member or the first argument is not a map. Distinguishes an absent member (empty list) from a member whose value is null (a list holding null), which plain indexing cannot. The map counterpart of get_child_by_name; lists use get_element_by_index.
    GetMemberByKey { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// Elements from start (inclusive) to end (exclusive) taking every step-th. Negative start and end count from the end of the list. A null step means 1; a null start or end means the beginning or end of the list in the direction of travel. A negative step walks backwards; a zero step yields the empty list. Out-of-range bounds are clamped, never an error. The semantics are those of RFC 9535 array slices. A non-list first argument yields the empty list.
    ListSlice { collection: Box<LogExpr>, start: Box<LogExpr>, end: Box<LogExpr>, step: Box<LogExpr> },
    Ln { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    Log10 { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    Ceil { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    Floor { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    Round { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// Parse a JSON string into a dynamically-typed value. Returns Any; caller must cast to a concrete type. JSON arrays become Array[Any], JSON objects become Map[String, Any].
    JsonParse { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// Parse a JSON object string into a StructType. Field names in the JSON become struct field names; types are inferred or declared by schema. The common case: a varchar column containing an escaped JSON document. Unlike JsonParse, the target struct type must be known at compile time.
    JsonParseStruct { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// serialize any value to a JSON string
    JsonStringify { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// Extract a value from a JSON string by JSONPath-like expression. First param is the JSON string, second is the path (e.g. "$.shipping.country"). Returns Any; avoids full parse when only one field is needed.
    JsonExtract { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// Like JsonExtract but always returns the result as a string, even for numbers/booleans. Matches Trino's json_extract_scalar behavior.
    JsonExtractString { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// Tests whether an IP address (first param) falls within a CIDR block (second param, e.g. "10.0.0.0/8"). Supports both IPv4 and IPv6. Addresses are strings; we may introduce a native IP type later.
    CidrContains { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// Tests whether an IP address matches any CIDR block in a list. Sugar for exists(cidrs, c, CidrContains(ip, c)) but evaluable with a radix tree for large block lists.
    CidrMatch { lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// parse IPv4 to u32 or IPv6 to u128; useful for range comparisons
    IpToInt { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    /// render integer as dotted-quad (v4) or colon-hex (v6)
    IntToIp { operand: Box<LogExpr> },

    JsonParseAs { target_type: meta_types::type_syntax::TypeLiteral, operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    GetFieldByName { field_name: String },
    GetFieldByIndex { field_index: u32 },
    GetChildByName { child_name: String, operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    GetChildByIndex { child_index: u32, lhs: Box<LogExpr>, rhs: Box<LogExpr> },

    Has { operand: Box<LogExpr> },
    All { collection: Box<LogExpr>, binding: String, body: Box<LogExpr> },
    Exists { collection: Box<LogExpr>, binding: String, body: Box<LogExpr> },
    ExistsOne { collection: Box<LogExpr>, binding: String, body: Box<LogExpr> },
    Filter { collection: Box<LogExpr>, binding: String, body: Box<LogExpr> },
    MapTransform { collection: Box<LogExpr>, binding: String, body: Box<LogExpr> },

    /// Opaque CEL sub-expression that could not be raised to a physical IR node.
    /// The `source` field is the reconstructed CEL text, kept for informational/
    /// debugging purposes ONLY — it must NEVER be re-parsed for execution.
    /// The authoritative representation is the compiled program in the side table.
    CelFallback { source: String, args: Vec<Box<LogExpr>> },

    /// Unresolved external UDF call (from CEL parse). Must be resolved
    /// against the query's import list before type checking.
    UnresolvedCall { name: String, args: Vec<Box<LogExpr>> },

    /// Resolved external UDF call with fully-qualified reference.
    ExternalCall { udf: meta_types::external_fn::ResolvedUdfRef, args: Vec<Box<LogExpr>> },

    /// Multi-way conditional (desugared CASE).
    Case { arms: Vec<(Box<LogExpr>, Box<LogExpr>)>, default: Box<LogExpr> },
}

/// Generated — do not modify. See top of file.
impl LogExpr {
    pub fn intrinsic_coeffects(&self) -> crate::coeffects::CoeffectSet {
        use crate::coeffects::CoeffectSet;
        match self {
            Self::GetFieldByName { .. } | Self::GetFieldByIndex { .. } => CoeffectSet::event_data(),
            Self::CelFallback { .. } => CoeffectSet::unknown(),
            Self::UnresolvedCall { .. } | Self::ExternalCall { .. } => {
                CoeffectSet::external_udf(crate::coeffects::UdfLanguage::Opaque)
            },
            Self::CurrentTimestamp { .. } => CoeffectSet::current_time(0),
            _ => CoeffectSet::default(),
        }
    }

    pub fn is_commutative(&self) -> bool {
        matches!(self,
            Self::LogicalOr { .. } |
            Self::LogicalAnd { .. } |
            Self::Equal { .. } |
            Self::NotEqual { .. } |
            Self::NullSafeEqual { .. } |
            Self::NullSafeNotEqual { .. } |
            Self::Add { .. } |
            Self::Multiply { .. }
        )
    }
}

/// Generated — do not modify. See top of file.
pub fn transitive_coeffects(expr: &LogExpr) -> crate::coeffects::CoeffectSet {
    let mut result = expr.intrinsic_coeffects();
    match expr {
        LogExpr::Literal(_) => {},
        LogExpr::GetFieldByName { .. } | LogExpr::GetFieldByIndex { .. } | LogExpr::CurrentTimestamp => {},
        LogExpr::LogicalNot { operand } | LogExpr::Negate { operand }
        | LogExpr::IsNull { operand } | LogExpr::IsNotNull { operand }
        | LogExpr::IsNan { operand } | LogExpr::IsFinite { operand } | LogExpr::IsInfinite { operand }
        | LogExpr::Abs { operand } | LogExpr::Sqrt { operand } | LogExpr::Exp { operand } | LogExpr::Sign { operand }
        | LogExpr::Size { operand } | LogExpr::Lower { operand } | LogExpr::Upper { operand } | LogExpr::Trim { operand }
        | LogExpr::TimestampExtract { operand } | LogExpr::RoundTemporal { operand } | LogExpr::RoundCalendar { operand }
        | LogExpr::CastBool { operand } | LogExpr::CastInt { operand } | LogExpr::CastUint { operand }
        | LogExpr::CastDouble { operand } | LogExpr::CastString { operand } | LogExpr::CastBytes { operand }
        | LogExpr::CastDuration { operand } | LogExpr::CastTimestamp { operand }
        | LogExpr::TypeOf { operand } | LogExpr::Dyn { operand }
        | LogExpr::Ln { operand } | LogExpr::Log10 { operand }
        | LogExpr::Ceil { operand } | LogExpr::Floor { operand } | LogExpr::Round { operand }
        | LogExpr::JsonParse { operand } | LogExpr::JsonParseStruct { operand } | LogExpr::JsonStringify { operand }
        | LogExpr::IpToInt { operand } | LogExpr::IntToIp { operand }
        | LogExpr::Has { operand }
        | LogExpr::Flatten { operand } | LogExpr::ListElements { operand } | LogExpr::MapValues { operand } | LogExpr::Descendants { operand }
        | LogExpr::RaiseError { operand }
        => { result = result.union(transitive_coeffects(operand)); },
        LogExpr::LogicalOr { lhs, rhs } | LogExpr::LogicalAnd { lhs, rhs }
        | LogExpr::Equal { lhs, rhs } | LogExpr::NotEqual { lhs, rhs }
        | LogExpr::LessThan { lhs, rhs } | LogExpr::LessOrEqual { lhs, rhs }
        | LogExpr::GreaterThan { lhs, rhs } | LogExpr::GreaterOrEqual { lhs, rhs }
        | LogExpr::NullSafeEqual { lhs, rhs } | LogExpr::NullSafeNotEqual { lhs, rhs }
        | LogExpr::Coalesce { lhs, rhs } | LogExpr::TryOrElse { lhs, rhs } | LogExpr::Least { lhs, rhs } | LogExpr::Greatest { lhs, rhs }
        | LogExpr::Add { lhs, rhs } | LogExpr::Subtract { lhs, rhs }
        | LogExpr::Multiply { lhs, rhs } | LogExpr::Divide { lhs, rhs } | LogExpr::Modulus { lhs, rhs }
        | LogExpr::Power { lhs, rhs }
        | LogExpr::StringSplit { lhs, rhs } | LogExpr::StringPosition { lhs, rhs } | LogExpr::Concat { lhs, rhs }
        | LogExpr::Index { lhs, rhs } | LogExpr::In { lhs, rhs }
        | LogExpr::JsonExtract { lhs, rhs } | LogExpr::JsonExtractString { lhs, rhs }
        | LogExpr::CidrContains { lhs, rhs } | LogExpr::CidrMatch { lhs, rhs }
        | LogExpr::RegexExtract { lhs, rhs }
        | LogExpr::ListAppend { lhs, rhs } | LogExpr::ListConcat { lhs, rhs } | LogExpr::GetElementByIndex { lhs, rhs } | LogExpr::GetMemberByKey { lhs, rhs }
        => {
            result = result.union(transitive_coeffects(lhs));
            result = result.union(transitive_coeffects(rhs));
        },
        LogExpr::Contains { receiver, arg } | LogExpr::StartsWith { receiver, arg }
        | LogExpr::EndsWith { receiver, arg } | LogExpr::RegexMatch { receiver, arg }
        => {
            result = result.union(transitive_coeffects(receiver));
            result = result.union(transitive_coeffects(arg));
        },
        LogExpr::Between { arg0, arg1, arg2 } | LogExpr::Substring { arg0, arg1, arg2 }
        | LogExpr::Replace { arg0, arg1, arg2 } | LogExpr::RegexReplace { arg0, arg1, arg2 }
        | LogExpr::UrlPathSegment { arg0, arg1, arg2 } | LogExpr::UrlQueryParam { arg0, arg1, arg2 }
        => {
            result = result.union(transitive_coeffects(arg0));
            result = result.union(transitive_coeffects(arg1));
            result = result.union(transitive_coeffects(arg2));
        },
        LogExpr::JsonParseAs { operand, .. } => { result = result.union(transitive_coeffects(operand)); },
        LogExpr::ListSlice { collection, start, end, step } => {
            result = result.union(transitive_coeffects(collection));
            result = result.union(transitive_coeffects(start));
            result = result.union(transitive_coeffects(end));
            result = result.union(transitive_coeffects(step));
        },
        LogExpr::Conditional { condition, then_expr, else_expr } => {
            result = result.union(transitive_coeffects(condition));
            result = result.union(transitive_coeffects(then_expr));
            result = result.union(transitive_coeffects(else_expr));
        },
        LogExpr::GetChildByName { operand, .. } => {
            result = result.union(transitive_coeffects(operand));
        },
        LogExpr::GetChildByIndex { lhs, rhs, .. } => {
            result = result.union(transitive_coeffects(lhs));
            result = result.union(transitive_coeffects(rhs));
        },
        LogExpr::All { collection, body, .. } | LogExpr::Exists { collection, body, .. }
        | LogExpr::ExistsOne { collection, body, .. } | LogExpr::Filter { collection, body, .. }
        | LogExpr::MapTransform { collection, body, .. }
        => {
            result = result.union(transitive_coeffects(collection));
            result = result.union(transitive_coeffects(body));
        },
        LogExpr::CelFallback { args, .. } | LogExpr::UnresolvedCall { args, .. } | LogExpr::ExternalCall { args, .. } => {
            for arg in args {
                result = result.union(transitive_coeffects(arg));
            }
        },
        LogExpr::Case { arms, default } => {
            for (cond, body) in arms {
                result = result.union(transitive_coeffects(cond));
                result = result.union(transitive_coeffects(body));
            }
            result = result.union(transitive_coeffects(default));
        },
    }
    result
}

/// Generated — do not modify. See top of file.
impl LogExpr {
    /// True if this expression tree can be evaluated at compile time --
    /// no event data, no session state, no aggregates, no enrichment.
    /// Useful for predicate pushdown: e.g. `IN (x, y, z)` can only be
    /// rewritten to a hash lookup if all elements are foldable.
    pub fn is_foldable(&self) -> bool {
        transitive_coeffects(self).is_pure()
    }
}

/// Generated — do not modify. See top of file.
impl LogExpr {
    /// Mutable references to this node's direct children, in field order.
    pub fn children_mut(&mut self) -> Vec<&mut LogExpr> {
        match self {
            Self::Literal(_) => vec![],
            Self::LogicalOr { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::LogicalAnd { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::LogicalNot { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::Equal { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::NotEqual { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::LessThan { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::LessOrEqual { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::GreaterThan { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::GreaterOrEqual { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::Between { arg0, arg1, arg2, .. } => vec![arg0.as_mut(), arg1.as_mut(), arg2.as_mut()],
            Self::NullSafeEqual { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::NullSafeNotEqual { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::IsNull { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::IsNotNull { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::IsNan { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::IsFinite { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::IsInfinite { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::Coalesce { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::TryOrElse { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::RaiseError { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::Least { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::Greatest { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::Add { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::Subtract { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::Multiply { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::Divide { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::Negate { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::Modulus { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::Abs { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::Power { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::Sqrt { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::Exp { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::Sign { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::Contains { receiver, arg, .. } => vec![receiver.as_mut(), arg.as_mut()],
            Self::StartsWith { receiver, arg, .. } => vec![receiver.as_mut(), arg.as_mut()],
            Self::EndsWith { receiver, arg, .. } => vec![receiver.as_mut(), arg.as_mut()],
            Self::RegexMatch { receiver, arg, .. } => vec![receiver.as_mut(), arg.as_mut()],
            Self::RegexExtract { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::RegexReplace { arg0, arg1, arg2, .. } => vec![arg0.as_mut(), arg1.as_mut(), arg2.as_mut()],
            Self::UrlPathSegment { arg0, arg1, arg2, .. } => vec![arg0.as_mut(), arg1.as_mut(), arg2.as_mut()],
            Self::UrlQueryParam { arg0, arg1, arg2, .. } => vec![arg0.as_mut(), arg1.as_mut(), arg2.as_mut()],
            Self::Size { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::Lower { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::Upper { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::Substring { arg0, arg1, arg2, .. } => vec![arg0.as_mut(), arg1.as_mut(), arg2.as_mut()],
            Self::Replace { arg0, arg1, arg2, .. } => vec![arg0.as_mut(), arg1.as_mut(), arg2.as_mut()],
            Self::Trim { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::StringSplit { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::StringPosition { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::Concat { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::TimestampExtract { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::RoundTemporal { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::RoundCalendar { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::CurrentTimestamp { .. } => vec![],
            Self::CastBool { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::CastInt { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::CastUint { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::CastDouble { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::CastString { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::CastBytes { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::CastDuration { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::CastTimestamp { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::TypeOf { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::Dyn { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::Conditional { condition, then_expr, else_expr, .. } => vec![condition.as_mut(), then_expr.as_mut(), else_expr.as_mut()],
            Self::Index { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::In { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::ListAppend { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::ListConcat { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::Flatten { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::ListElements { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::MapValues { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::Descendants { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::GetElementByIndex { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::GetMemberByKey { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::ListSlice { collection, start, end, step, .. } => vec![collection.as_mut(), start.as_mut(), end.as_mut(), step.as_mut()],
            Self::Ln { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::Log10 { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::Ceil { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::Floor { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::Round { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::JsonParse { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::JsonParseStruct { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::JsonStringify { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::JsonExtract { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::JsonExtractString { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::CidrContains { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::CidrMatch { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::IpToInt { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::IntToIp { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::JsonParseAs { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::GetFieldByName { .. } => vec![],
            Self::GetFieldByIndex { .. } => vec![],
            Self::GetChildByName { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::GetChildByIndex { lhs, rhs, .. } => vec![lhs.as_mut(), rhs.as_mut()],
            Self::Has { operand, .. } => vec![operand.as_mut()],
            Self::All { collection, body, .. } => vec![collection.as_mut(), body.as_mut()],
            Self::Exists { collection, body, .. } => vec![collection.as_mut(), body.as_mut()],
            Self::ExistsOne { collection, body, .. } => vec![collection.as_mut(), body.as_mut()],
            Self::Filter { collection, body, .. } => vec![collection.as_mut(), body.as_mut()],
            Self::MapTransform { collection, body, .. } => vec![collection.as_mut(), body.as_mut()],
            Self::CelFallback { args, .. } | Self::UnresolvedCall { args, .. } | Self::ExternalCall { args, .. } => {
                args.iter_mut().map(|a| a.as_mut()).collect()
            }
            Self::Case { arms, default } => {
                let mut v = Vec::with_capacity(arms.len() * 2 + 1);
                for (c, r) in arms.iter_mut() {
                    v.push(c.as_mut());
                    v.push(r.as_mut());
                }
                v.push(default.as_mut());
                v
            }
        }
    }

    /// This node's own type-literal properties (not its children's).
    pub fn type_literals_mut(&mut self) -> Vec<&mut meta_types::type_syntax::TypeLiteral> {
        match self {
            Self::JsonParseAs { target_type, .. } => vec![target_type],
            _ => vec![],
        }
    }
}
